h: Getting the most out of a Milton Keynes visit
p: With sessions that aren't time-limited, you can be flexible and let the kids set the pace. Some families do a big morning of play then head off for lunch, others pop in for a calmer afternoon once the morning rush has passed. Either way, you won't be clock-watching.

Think about the ages in your group. Babies and young toddlers often love the gentler sensory and role-play bits, while older primary children usually want to climb, race and try the dodgems. If you've got a mix, bring a second grown-up if possible so one can stay with the little one while the other follows the bigger kids around.
Pack a bag with socks for everyone, spare clothes, a towel and a drink bottle each. Messy and water play are a lot more fun when you're not worried about what the kids are wearing.

Milton Keynes has heaps of family days out beyond the play centre. Bletchley Park, where codebreakers worked in secret during the Second World War, is fascinating for older kids and grown-ups alike. Keep an eye out for the famous Concrete Cows, a quirky local landmark that's become a symbol of the town.
Xscape in the centre of town is home to an indoor real-snow slope, which is a fun treat if you've got skiers or snowboarders in the family, alongside other leisure options.
For a quieter run-around, the Grand Union Canal winds through the area, with towpath walks perfect for spotting narrowboats and ducks, and there are plenty of parks dotted around the town.
